def load() -> pd.DataFrame:
    import glob
    import pandas as pd

    pattern = "data/legal/input/csn-data-book-2024-csv/CSVs/State MSA Identity Theft data/*.csv"
    paths = sorted(glob.glob(pattern))
    if not paths:
        raise FileNotFoundError(f"No files matched pattern: {pattern}")

    dfs = []
    for p in paths:
        # Files in this folder are expected to be tabular CSVs with a header row.
        df = pd.read_csv(p)
        df["_source_file"] = p.split("/")[-1]
        dfs.append(df)

    out = pd.concat(dfs, ignore_index=True, sort=False)
    return out

def process(loadMsaIdentityTheft2024) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = loadMsaIdentityTheft2024.copy()

    metro_col = 'Metropolitan Areas: Identity Theft Reports'
    reports_col = 'Unnamed: 1'

    out = df[[metro_col, reports_col, '_source_file']].rename(
        columns={metro_col: 'metropolitan_area', reports_col: 'reports_raw'}
    )

    out['metropolitan_area'] = out['metropolitan_area'].astype('string').fillna('').str.strip()
    rep = out['reports_raw'].astype('string').fillna('').str.strip()

    # Drop headers/footers/blanks
    is_blank = out['metropolitan_area'].eq('')
    is_header = out['metropolitan_area'].str.fullmatch(r'(?i)metropolitan\s+area', na=False)
    is_source = out['metropolitan_area'].str.match(r'(?i)^source:', na=False)

    out = out.loc[~(is_blank | is_header | is_source)].copy()

    # Parse report counts
    rep = rep.loc[out.index]
    rep = rep.replace({'': pd.NA, 'nan': pd.NA, 'N/A': pd.NA, 'NA': pd.NA, '-': pd.NA})
    rep = rep.str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
    out['reports'] = pd.to_numeric(rep.str.extract(r'(\d+)', expand=False), errors='coerce')

    out = out.dropna(subset=['reports'])

    return out[['metropolitan_area', 'reports', '_source_file']].reset_index(drop=True)

def process(loadMsaIdentityTheft2024) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = loadMsaIdentityTheft2024.copy()
    metro_col = 'Metropolitan Areas: Identity Theft Reports'
    reports_col = 'Unnamed: 1'

    out = df[[metro_col, reports_col, '_source_file']].rename(
        columns={metro_col: 'metropolitan_area', reports_col: 'reports_raw'}
    )

    out['metro_str'] = out['metropolitan_area'].astype('string')
    out['metro_norm'] = out['metro_str'].fillna('').str.strip()

    rep = out['reports_raw'].astype('string')
    out['rep_norm'] = rep.fillna('').str.strip()
    out['rep_norm_nocomma'] = out['rep_norm'].str.replace(',', '', regex=False)
    out['rep_num_extracted'] = out['rep_norm_nocomma'].str.extract(r'(\d+)', expand=False)

    looks_like_msa = out['metro_norm'].str.contains('Metropolitan Statistical Area', case=False, na=False)
    sample = out.loc[looks_like_msa, ['_source_file','metropolitan_area','reports_raw','rep_norm','rep_num_extracted']].head(50)

    bad = (
        out['metro_norm'].eq('')
        | out['metro_norm'].str.match(r'(?i)^source:')
        | out['metro_norm'].eq('Metropolitan Area')
    )
    dropped_examples = out.loc[bad, ['_source_file','metropolitan_area','reports_raw']].head(20)

    # Ensure we always return a non-empty schema even if samples are empty.
    if sample.empty and dropped_examples.empty:
        return pd.DataFrame(columns=['_section','_source_file','metropolitan_area','reports_raw','rep_norm','rep_num_extracted'])

    return pd.concat([
        sample.assign(_section='looks_like_msa').reset_index(drop=True),
        dropped_examples.assign(_section='dropped_examples').reset_index(drop=True)
    ], ignore_index=True)

def process(cleanMsaIdentityTheft2024) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd
    import re

    df = cleanMsaIdentityTheft2024.copy()

    # Metropolitan Statistical Areas only (exclude micropolitan)
    msa = df[df['metropolitan_area'].str.contains(r'Metropolitan Statistical Area', case=False, na=False)].copy()

    # Cross-state MSAs in this CSN table are denoted by state abbreviation pairs joined by a hyphen, e.g., PA-NJ
    # (Some MSAs may contain multiple states like DC-VA-MD-WV; the hyphen pattern will still match.)
    cross_state = msa[msa['metropolitan_area'].str.contains(r'\b[A-Z]{2}(?:-[A-Z]{2})+\b', regex=True, na=False)].copy()

    total = pd.to_numeric(cross_state['reports'], errors='coerce').sum()

    return pd.DataFrame({'total_identity_theft_reports_2024_cross_state_msa': [int(total)]})

def process(cleanMsaIdentityTheft2024) -> pd.DataFrame:
    import pandas as pd

    df = cleanMsaIdentityTheft2024.copy()

    # Focus on Metropolitan Statistical Areas
    msa = df[df['metropolitan_area'].str.contains(r'Metropolitan Statistical Area', case=False, na=False)].copy()

    # Candidate cross-state patterns commonly used in CSN tables
    patterns = [
        r'\b[A-Z]{2}\s*/\s*[A-Z]{2}\b',           # TX/AR
        r'\b[A-Z]{2}-[A-Z]{2}\b',                 # TX-AR
        r'\b[A-Z]{2}\s*&\s*[A-Z]{2}\b',         # TX & AR
        r'\b[A-Z]{2}\s+and\s+[A-Z]{2}\b',       # TX and AR
    ]

    cand = msa.copy()
    mask = False
    for pat in patterns:
        mask = mask | cand['metropolitan_area'].str.contains(pat, regex=True, na=False)
    cand = cand[mask].copy()

    # If still empty, return most suspicious names containing multiple commas (often multiple states)
    if cand.empty:
        cand = msa[msa['metropolitan_area'].str.count(',') >= 2].copy()

    # Return a sample plus counts
    out = cand[['metropolitan_area', 'reports', '_source_file']].sort_values('metropolitan_area')
    out = out.head(200)

    return out.reset_index(drop=True)

If none found, fall back to names with >=2 commas; return up to 200 candidate rows with metropolitan_area, reports, _source_file for pattern inspection.
